verdicts.quote: Automatic, first-come-first-served promotion is the proposed product default. … For each admission, create an ordinary confirmed booking and end its active entry as **Promoted** as one business outcome.

Automatic, first-come-first-served promotion … Simultaneous joins by distinct members acquire a unique order as accepted by the booking authority, even when timestamps coincide. … Manual queue overrides, special priority tiers, … are outside this scope.
Promotion uses the existing booking identity and terms. … A later ordinary cancellation of the promoted booking does not rejoin the queue.
verdicts.missing: Promotion is automatic, so there is no offer to decline. The text does not say whether missing the class or cancelling late after automatic promotion incurs the existing penalty.

verdicts.quote: Cancellation of a confirmed booking, a capacity increase, or any other supported change that makes seats allocatable serves the earliest still-eligible entries first. … its effect must be recoverable without either member's client
verdicts.missing: How soon allocation must finish after a cancellation if the seat release commits first.

verdicts.quote: A fresh read shows **Booked** in class details and the booking area even if the member's app was closed. … No new accounts, public roster, or off-app message delivery is required.
verdicts.missing: The member can see the result on a read. There is no specified delivery or failure behavior for a promotion notice sent to the member.

verdicts.quote: Simultaneous leaves, releases, bookings, and closure resolve in one authoritative order for the occurrence. … Duplicate or stale release processing cannot issue extra bookings, reuse a released seat, re-promote a terminal entry, or restore an older status.
An ordinary booking competing for a released seat can succeed only after the eligible queue receives its priority and capacity remains.
verdicts.missing: What the direct booking request returns when its own member has just been promoted, and how a second booking for that member is prevented if another seat remains.

verdicts.quote: If an ordinary booking requires a fresh member choice, payment authorization, or terms acceptance, automatic promotion for that class type is unready.
verdicts.missing: When to authorize or collect payment and what happens to the booking, queue entry and seat if payment fails.

verdicts.quote: The request supplies no active-entry count limit. If the runtime needs one, product must decide the applicable bound and the Join behavior at it before that path is planned.
verdicts.missing: Whether there is a cap, its value if imposed, and what the member sees when it is reached.

verdicts.quote: Existing cutoff or scheduled start, whichever comes first, or authorized cancellation. … Before the cutoff an open occurrence can admit or promote under R-1 and R-3. At the cutoff and later it cannot.

a capacity increase, or any other supported change that makes seats allocatable serves the earliest still-eligible entries first. … If the baseline permits an over-capacity state through a capacity decrease, promotion stops until there is allocatable capacity.
On occurrence cancellation, end them with **Class canceled**. Clear rank and remove the actionable Join and Leave controls for ended entries.

The booking authority owns active membership and its ordering for the existing member × occurrence identity. … Reads derive current rank from committed active order. … Append once to active order and return current own Waitlisted status.
verdicts.missing: Whether each entry records its join time alongside its state and ordering information.

verdicts.quote: At the cutoff, end remaining active entries with **Waitlist closed**. … Cleanup removes expired terminal and replay information under the existing retention and deletion policy.
verdicts.missing: The retention period or expiry event for terminal entries after the class runs.

verdicts.quote: A current authorized read shows the member's one-based rank among active entries. … A member without an active entry receives no rank, and no read exposes another member's identity.
Manual queue overrides, special priority tiers, timed offers, penalties, and a new outbound notification system are outside this scope. … Operational access stays within existing roles and purpose.
verdicts.missing: Manual overrides are excluded. The text does not establish a staff queue view or a staff-accessible history identifying each promoted member and the promotion time.

verdicts.quote: Open bounds are supported occurrence and queue sizes, per-occurrence contention and independent-occurrence load, service or storage quotas, mutation/read freshness, and allocation/reconciliation delay. No numeric target was supplied.
verdicts.missing: The maximum elapsed time from a committed cancellation to promotion.
